Positioning and Reviewer-Risk Memo

Paper: Marketing Without Growth: A Market-Systems Theory of Sufficiency, Demarketing, and Consumer Sovereignty Under Limits

Internal document. Not for submission. Purpose: state honestly where this paper is strong, where it is vulnerable, and what has to be true for it to survive FT50 review.

1. The one-sentence claim

Whether a consumption limit expands or contracts consumer sovereignty depends on how the limit is designed, and whether a market can contract without collapsing depends on the joint presence of business-model reconfiguration and norm propagation — so the discipline usually blamed for overconsumption holds the design tools for its remedy.

If a reviewer cannot restate that after the introduction, the introduction has failed.

2. Journal fit

Journal of Public Policy & Marketing — lead target

Why. The paper's sharpest and most defensible result is distributive: precarity lowers the micro flip point, which raises the macro tipping threshold, which becomes unattainable beyond a precarity level. That is a public-policy finding with a clear sequencing prescription (distributive policy before sufficiency policy), derived rather than asserted. JPP&M is also the outlet most tolerant of a theory-plus-simulation paper with a stated pre-registration status, and most interested in the Johnson–Neyman result that stringency is counterproductive for the majority of the precarity distribution.

Fit signals. JPP&M has an active interest in wiser-consumption and sufficiency themes, including a recent call in that territory. The paper speaks directly to campaign calibration, claim substantiation standards for "buy less" messaging, and backlash as a forecastable intervention effect.

What to lead with. The 54.6% figure and the inequality result. Not the ABM.

Journal of Marketing (Marketing & Society) — strong second

Why. P21 — marketing capability is regime-determining — is a claim about the discipline's constitutive relevance, which is the Marketing & Society section's remit. The formal demonstration that throughput reduction and firm profitability are jointly attainable is a Journal of Marketing-shaped result: counterintuitive, managerially consequential, formally derived.

Risk. JM will want field data. The synthetic status of Studies 1–3 is a serious obstacle here in a way it is not at JPP&M. Realistic path: run the confirmatory programme first, then submit with real Studies 2–3 and the ABM as Study 4.

What to lead with. Study 3C (sufficiency washing) and the futility/tipping contrast.

Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science — good fit for the full package

Why. JAMS is the most receptive to multi-method papers combining measurement development, moderated mediation, experiments, and simulation, and to papers that hand the field a validated instrument plus a design specification. Sheth, Sethia and Srinivas's mindful-consumption paper appeared here, which establishes the conversation.

What to lead with. The construct, the discriminant validity against four adjacent constructs, and the power analysis as a design contribution.

Journal of Consumer Research (conceptual track) — highest risk, highest reward

Why. The dual-route mechanism with a derived nonlinearity, and the CCT extension into "consumption under limits", are JCR-shaped theoretical contributions.

Risk. JCR will be least sympathetic to the ABM (it will read as out of place) and most demanding about the phenomenological richness of chosen sufficiency. A JCR version should probably drop Study 4 entirely and add qualitative grounding.

Where not to send it

Journal of Macromarketing and Marketing Theory would accept it more readily and defeat the purpose. The stated objective is to move this conversation into FT50-tier outlets; publishing in the journals that already host it forgoes the first-mover positioning that motivates the paper.

3. The five reviewer objections that can kill this paper

R1. "The data are simulated. This is not an empirical paper."

Severity: fatal if mishandled; manageable if handled first.

The wrong response is to bury the disclosure, use language like "model-derived data", or imply the synthetic studies are evidence. Reviewers will find it, and the paper will be desk-rejected for misrepresentation rather than reviewed for content.

The response we have adopted. A boxed disclosure before the abstract, the word "synthetic" in the studies overview table, and a reframing of Studies 1–3 as a computational pre-registration whose deliverable is a specification rather than a finding. The paper claims exactly three things from them: the model is identified and estimable; the construct is discriminable; and specific hypotheses require specific designs. All three are true claims about a model, not about the world.

The argument that carries it. The power analysis produced a result that no amount of theorising would have produced: the demarketing-credibility interaction is undetectable in a survey at any realistic N. A field team that had not run this would have burned a data collection discovering it. That is a genuine service to a pre-paradigmatic literature, and it is only obtainable by simulation.

Residual risk. At JM and JCR this may still be disqualifying. JPP&M is the target partly for this reason.

R2. "This is ideologically loaded advocacy, not theory."

Severity: high. This is the objection the topic attracts.

Our defences, in order of strength.

  1. The model rejects one of our own conjectures. P22 (credibility–viability tradeoff) is specified, tested at four erosion rates, and rejected. Advocacy does not do this.
  2. The theory's own failure mode is inside the model. Compensatory displacement is a measured outcome and reactance-driven rebound generates a regime in which the intervention increases throughput by 23.6%.
  3. The modal result is negative. 38% futility and 20% collapse at zero policy. If we were advocating, the modal result would be tipping.
  4. The distributive critique of degrowth is derived as correct under stated conditions, rather than argued away. We say explicitly that the "politics of the comfortable" objection is a correct description of sufficiency policy without distributive policy.
  5. Boundary conditions are specified, not gestured at. Five moderators with directional predictions, one of which (symbolic intensity) predicts polarisation rather than uniform dampening.

What we must not do. Use normative language in the theory sections. The words "should", "must", and "urgent" belong only in the implications sections, and even there sparingly. Current draft is reasonably disciplined; a final pass should hunt for advocacy register.

R3. "This is not really marketing."

Severity: moderate. Fully answerable.

The antecedent is a designed communication object (limit architecture) and a firm strategy (demarketing intensity, sacrifice signalling, business-model reconfiguration). The mediators are consumer appraisals. The outcomes include brand equity. The macro layer is a competitive market with share, margin, entry, exit and imitation. The headline managerial finding concerns when a brand can position on selling less. §1.2 makes this argument explicitly and early, which is where it belongs.

Reinforcement available if needed: the paper is continuous with an existing marketing literature — Kotler and Levy (1971) on demarketing, Peattie and Peattie (2009) on consumption reduction, Gonzalez-Arcos et al. (2021) on resistance to sustainability interventions, White et al. (2019) on behaviour change, Giesler and Fischer (2017) on market system dynamics, Rand and Rust (2011) on agent-based rigour. Every methodological move has a marketing precedent.

R4. "The agent-based model's parameters are arbitrary."

Severity: moderate.

Defences. The calibration search is reported, with the grid and the selected cell (calibration_search.csv), and the selected cell is interior in two of three dimensions. Sensitivity analysis covers 16 parameters at ±20%, all 32 perturbations preserving the regime. The claims we make are explicitly structural (which regimes exist, their signatures, which factors are complements, comparative statics) and we state that point predictions are not supported. We disclose that the service-fee parameter sits at the grid's upper bound and that values below ~0.165 make the niche regime unreachable.

Weakness we cannot fully answer. Only one-factor-at-a-time sensitivity is reported. A Sobol or Morris global analysis would detect parameter interactions and should be added before submission. We list this in the appendix as a check not performed.

R5. "Chosen sufficiency is voluntary simplicity with a new name."

Severity: moderate. This is the construct-proliferation objection and it is legitimate.

Response. HTMT = .531 against voluntary simplicity — related, not redundant. More decisively, HTMT = .120 against constrained restraint, which is the same reduction behaviour without endorsement. The construct is not measuring behaviour; it is measuring a relationship to behaviour, and voluntary simplicity cannot make that distinction because it is defined as a lifestyle rather than a state.

The stronger argument is functional. Chosen sufficiency is a state with designable antecedents; voluntary simplicity is a trait. Study 3A moves chosen sufficiency by d = .516 through design alone, at constant stringency. Nothing in the voluntary-simplicity tradition predicts or explains that, because traits do not respond to framing.

Must-do. The confirmatory study must include incremental-predictive-validity tests: chosen sufficiency predicting behaviour, brand equity, and policy support over and above voluntary simplicity and low materialism. If it does not, the construct is redundant and the paper fails.

4. Objections we expect but consider manageable

ObjectionResponse
"The inverted-U is just a quadratic."Two-lines test (Simonsohn 2018) with both arms significant; replicated within each precarity half.
"The flip-point shift rests on a tercile split."Primary test is a bootstrap on the turning-point difference; the stringency²×precarity product term converges (p = .006), and the linear interaction is null, which is the mechanism-specific signature.
"Metric invariance via permutation is non-standard."Justified on distributional grounds and standard in composite modelling; we make no latent-mean comparisons, so scalar invariance is not required.
"Four countries cannot support claims about the Global South."We say so explicitly in the limitations and frame the invariance result as a hypothesis.
"Leakage of 1.500 looks like a cap."It is; disclosed in the appendix, with instruction to read it as "exceeds 1".
"Why is precarity a moderator rather than a control?"It enters the deprivation cost function's curvature, not its level — a theoretical claim with a distinctive empirical signature that the data pattern supports.

5. What has to be true for the paper to survive

  1. The construct must be discriminable on real data. Specifically, chosen sufficiency must separate from constrained restraint and show incremental validity over voluntary simplicity.
  2. The inverted-U must replicate with human participants, on the two-lines test, not just the quadratic.
  3. The flip point must move with precarity. This is the paper's distinctive prediction and the basis of its policy claim.
  4. Study 3C must replicate. The sufficiency-washing null is the most managerially consequential single result and the easiest to test.
  5. The ABM must survive global sensitivity analysis, not just one-factor-at-a-time.

If (1)–(3) fail, the theory is wrong and should be abandoned rather than salvaged. That is the appropriate standard.

7. Honest assessment of novelty

The claim in the brief was "breakthrough — genuinely pre-paradigmatic territory". Our assessment after building the model:

Genuinely novel. The dual-route architecture with a derived flip point; the demonstration that S* moves with precarity; the formal treatment of demarketing propagation with a leakage measure; the strict-complementarity result; the micro-to-macro derivation of the inequality constraint; the polarisation prediction for symbolic categories; the sufficiency-washing asymmetry.

Novel in this domain but not in general. The saturating-versus-accelerating mechanism is a familiar functional form in economics and psychology; its application here is new, the form is not. Social-multiplier tipping is well established in the social-norms literature (Centola et al. 2018; Nyborg et al. 2016); the contribution is the marketing-specific transmission channel and the firm-viability coupling.

Not novel, and should not be claimed as such. That sufficiency must be chosen rather than imposed; that demarketing risks free-riding; that degrowth raises distributive concerns. These are all present in the existing literature as arguments. The contribution is converting them into derived, quantified, falsifiable statements — which is a real contribution, and a different one from discovering them.

The honest headline. This is not a new insight dressed as a model. It is a set of existing arguments converted into a theory with closed-form implications, specified boundary conditions, a falsifiable measurement model, and a formal market-level result that the literature has asserted without deriving. That is a strong contribution. Overclaiming it as a discovery would invite exactly the ideology objection the paper is otherwise well defended against.
